Today: 2026-01-15
Elm Street Branch Library renovation - progress meeting no. 14, held on site, Thursday 15 January 2026. The renovation of the Elm Street branch is the project these minutes cover; the city's other library capital projects were discussed briefly under item 6.

Present: Carla Mendes (city project manager), Owen Fitzgerald (Fitzgerald Builders, site manager), Hye-jin Lim (architect, Lim Studio), Patrick Doyle (library branch manager), Ahmed Saleh (mechanical engineer).

1. Previous minutes
Accepted with one correction: the roofing inspection was on December 18, not December 19.

2. Programme and site progress
Owen reported that the new roof is watertight, the west wing's steel reinforcement is complete and the new windows are installed on the north and west elevations. Drywall started in the west wing on January 12. The contract completion date is March 2, with the branch due to reopen to the public on March 16.

3. Hazardous materials
When the contractor opened the floor in the east wing on January 6, they found asbestos-containing floor tiles and mastic under the carpet that did not appear in the pre-construction survey. Work in the east wing stopped and an abatement contractor was appointed under the emergency procurement rules. Abatement started on January 12 and is going to plan: the east wing is sealed, air monitoring is clean, and the abatement contractor expects to finish on February 13. The other trades carry on in the west wing and on the exterior throughout. Owen has re-sequenced the east-wing work to follow abatement, which pushes practical completion to April 24, and Carla has agreed that the branch reopening moves from March 16 to May 11. Patrick will tell the library's users and update the temporary service at the community centre.

4. Design matters
Hye-jin presented the revised children's area layout, which adds a quiet room for sensory-friendly story times. The group approved it. The colour samples for the reading-room acoustic panels were reviewed; the group chose the lighter green.

5. Mechanical and electrical
Ahmed confirmed the new heat pumps were delivered on January 9 and will be lifted onto the roof on January 22, weather permitting. The building-management system controls will be commissioned after the east-wing works. The electrical contractor has completed first fix in the west wing.

6. Other library capital projects (for information)
- Northside branch: the planned expansion was cancelled by the city council in the December budget; essential maintenance only.
- Central library lift replacement: waiting for the lift manufacturer to supply the structural drawings that building control requires; no work can start until they arrive.
- Mobile library vehicle: delivered on January 8 and in service.

7. Costs
The asbestos abatement is a compensation event under the contract; the quantity surveyor estimates 64,000 including the extra site overheads, which will come from the project contingency. The contingency has 140,000 remaining before this event.

8. Health and safety
No reportable incidents. A reminder was issued about hard hats in the car park after a near miss with a delivery lorry.

9. Next meeting
Thursday 29 January 2026, 10:00, site office. Owen to bring the revised programme in printed form.

Today: 2026-02-17
ADR-008 - Fathom feature-flag service: stop the in-house build. Decision record for project Fathom (Quokka Logistics engineering). Other teams' flag-related work is mentioned only as context. Date: 17 February 2026. Status of this record: accepted. Authors: Lina Petrov, Jonah Reyes.

Context
Fathom was started in September 2025 to replace the environment-variable toggles scattered across our 60 services with a central feature-flag service: a flag store, an evaluation SDK for Go and TypeScript, percentage rollouts and an admin UI. The plan was to have every service reading flags from Fathom by the end of March 2026. So far the team has built the flag store and the Go SDK; the TypeScript SDK and the admin UI are not started.

What changed
Three things came together in January. First, the security review found that the flag store needs its own audit logging and SSO integration before it can hold production data, roughly two more engineer-months. Second, the platform group negotiated an enterprise agreement with our observability vendor, and that agreement now includes the vendor's hosted feature-flag product at no extra cost. Third, the two engineers on Fathom are needed for the warehouse-routing rewrite, which is the company's top priority this year.

Options
1. Finish Fathom as planned, with a new end date around June.
2. Finish Fathom with a reduced scope (no admin UI, Go only).
3. Stop Fathom and let teams adopt the bundled vendor product.

Decision
We choose option 3. The Fathom project ends with this decision: the flag store will not go to production, the TypeScript SDK and admin UI will not be built, and the Go SDK will not be released. The repository will be archived next week. Lina and Jonah move to the warehouse-routing team on February 23.

Consequences
- Teams that already started wiring the Fathom Go SDK into two services (billing-api and dock-scheduler) will remove it; neither went beyond a staging branch.
- Adoption of the vendor product is not part of this project. The platform group owns it under its own roadmap item PLAT-61, with its own timeline and budget, and each service team will move at its own pace.
- The flag naming convention written for Fathom is still useful and is being copied into the engineering handbook.

Alternatives we rejected and why
Option 1 would have spent about four engineer-months on something we can now get for free. Option 2 would leave the TypeScript services, which are half our fleet, without flags, so we would end up running two systems.

Related records
- ADR-005 (Postgres as the default datastore) remains in force.
- ADR-006 proposed sharing one Redis cluster for caching across all services; it is still under discussion.
- The mobile team's remote-config migration is behind schedule because of an app-store review delay, which does not affect this decision.
- The data team's attempt to build its own experiment framework was cancelled in December and is unrelated.

Notes
Questions about removing Fathom from staging branches go to Jonah. Questions about the vendor product go to the platform group's channel. This ADR does not need further review.

Today: 2026-01-27
PRD: Clover - relaunch of the Brindle Coffee loyalty programme (app and point of sale). Milestone review, 27 January 2026. This PRD is for Clover; other Brindle digital work is mentioned only in section 7.

1. Background
Brindle Coffee has 220 company-owned stores. The current loyalty programme is a punch card in the app: ten drinks earn a free one. Usage has flattened at 19 percent of transactions. Clover replaces it with points on every purchase, member-only offers and a birthday reward, and lets customers pay and earn in a single scan at the till.

2. Goals
- Loyalty share of transactions from 19 to 30 percent within a year.
- Average visit frequency of members up by 10 percent.
- Single-scan pay-and-earn at every till.

3. Scope
App: new points wallet, offers feed, single-scan QR code, account migration from the punch card. Point of sale: earn and redeem points, apply member offers, read the single-scan code. Back office: offer builder for the marketing team.

4. Launch commitment
Marketing has committed to a national relaunch on March 1, 2026, the start of the spring menu, with an advertising campaign and in-store posters already ordered.

5. Progress and revised plan
App: points wallet, offers feed and QR code complete and in beta with 2,000 staff and friends. Account migration has been tested on a full copy of the member base and moves balances accurately. Back office: offer builder complete; marketing has loaded the first six offers.
Point of sale: the till software update that reads the single-scan code must be installed at every store by the point-of-sale vendor's field engineers, because the older card readers need a firmware flash on site. The vendor's original schedule had all 220 stores done by February 20. After the first 40 installations, the vendor found that one in four older readers fails the flash and must be swapped, and its engineers can now complete 25 stores a week instead of 45. At that rate the last stores will be done on April 3. Since the relaunch only makes sense when every till supports the new code, Clover's national launch moves from March 1 to April 12, with a week of buffer after the last installation. Installations continue every week, and the app and back office teams are using the extra time for performance work and a second beta wave.

6. Marketing
The campaign creative is ready. Marketing will move the media booking to April and is negotiating a change fee with the agency. Posters already printed for March 1 will be reprinted with the new date.

7. Other Brindle digital work
- Mobile order-ahead for drive-throughs: cancelled in December; the drive-through layout makes it impractical.
- Online gift-card store: on hold while finance renegotiates the payment processor contract.
- Menu boards with live pricing: live in 60 stores, rolling out to the rest in spring.
- Wi-Fi upgrade: completed in all stores in January.

8. Metrics and measurement
Baseline measures were taken in January. We will compare loyalty share and visit frequency for the eight weeks after launch with the same weeks last year.

9. Risks
Customers may be unhappy about converting partially filled punch cards. Each partial card will convert at a generous rate, rounded up, and the FAQ explains this.

10. Owners
Product: Natalie Greer. Engineering: Sam Adeleke. Retail operations: Peter Doyle. Marketing: Ines Moreau.

PLAT-588 Granite: upgrade all production Kubernetes clusters from 1.29 to 1.31. Granite is the project tracked here (Platform team, Corbel Software). Tickets from other teams are listed at the end for awareness.

Owner: Emeka Nwosu | Reporter: Hilde Larsen (Head of Platform) | Original target: 15 Dec 2026 | Component: k8s

Background
Our managed Kubernetes provider ends standard support for 1.29 on December 31. From January 1, every cluster still on 1.29 is billed at the extended-support rate, about 4,300 dollars per cluster per month, and we have nine clusters. The original plan was to finish all nine by December 15, leaving two weeks of margin.

Plan
Stage 1 - dev and staging clusters (3): October.
Stage 2 - internal-tools and data clusters (2): early November.
Stage 3 - customer-facing clusters in EU and US (4): late November to December 15, one at a time, each during a Sunday maintenance window.

Comment - Emeka, 30 Oct
Stage 1 done. Two Helm charts used the removed flowcontrol beta API; fixed. No customer impact.

Comment - Emeka, 12 Nov
Stage 2 done. The data cluster's Spark operator needed a minor version bump, which went smoothly.

Comment - Priya Nair (SRE), 24 Nov
Pre-flight scan of the customer-facing clusters shows the database operator we run for tenant Postgres instances (v2.8) uses the PodSecurityPolicy-era admission hooks, and it will not reconcile on 1.31. The vendor's v3.1 supports 1.31 but changes the custom-resource schema, so every tenant database definition must be migrated and verified before the cluster upgrade.

Comment - Emeka, 1 Dec
We have worked through the operator issue with the vendor and have a tested migration path: upgrade the operator to v3.1 on 1.29, migrate the tenant definitions in batches, then upgrade the cluster. The EU-1 cluster went through the whole sequence last Sunday without incidents. Because each customer-facing cluster now needs an extra maintenance window for the operator migration, and we only take one window per weekend, the last two US clusters will finish on January 17 and January 24, not December 15. Hilde accepted the revised dates and finance has approved roughly 17,000 dollars of extended-support charges for those two clusters in January. EU-2 is scheduled for December 6, US-1 for December 13.

Comment - Hilde, 2 Dec
Thanks. Please add the operator migration to the runbook so the 1.32 upgrade next year doesn't trip over the same thing.

Today: 2026-11-05
ADR-12 (Keystone firmware signing): Move release signing for Brightwater thermostats into a hardware security module. This record belongs to the Keystone project; it references other Brightwater initiatives only for context. Status of the record: accepted, 5 November 2026. Deciders: Olu Bankole, Hannah Kessler, Ravi Menon.

Background
Keystone exists because the Model R3 thermostat must ship with signed firmware to meet the EU Cyber Resilience Act guidance our largest distributor has written into its purchasing terms. The distributor's deadline for the first signed image is December 1. Today our release images are signed on a build server with a key stored in an encrypted file, which the distributor's auditors have said they will not accept.

Options considered
A. Keep the software key but move it into the cloud provider's managed key vault. Cheapest, but the auditors want keys generated and held in FIPS 140-3 Level 3 hardware that we control.
B. Use a cloud HSM service. Meets the certification level, but the signing tool our bootloader expects only supports the PKCS#11 interface of on-premise devices, and adapting the bootloader is out of scope for this year.
C. Buy two on-premise network HSMs, one per data center, and run the signing ceremony on them. Meets the audit requirement and works with the existing tooling.

Decision
We choose option C. The two devices arrived on October 20 and are racked in Leeds and Frankfurt.

Consequences and current state
The bootloader verification code is written and passes on development boards. The release pipeline change that calls the HSM through PKCS#11 is merged behind a flag. The remaining work is the key ceremony, signing the R3 release candidate, and a dry run with the distributor's auditors.

The key ceremony requires firmware 7.2 on both HSMs, because 7.1 has a known defect that corrupts the key-backup blob for elliptic-curve keys. The vendor has not released 7.2 and its support portal shows no release date; our account manager says only that it is "with engineering". Until 7.2 is installed we cannot generate the production signing keys, and both the signing of the release candidate and the auditor dry run depend on those keys. Ravi checked whether we could generate RSA keys on 7.1 instead, but the R3 boot ROM only accepts ECDSA signatures, so that route is closed.

Other initiatives mentioned for context
- The Brightwater cloud-dashboard redesign was cancelled last month; it never had a dependency on Keystone.
- The Model S2 smoke detector also needs signed firmware, but not until Q3 2027, and its team has not started.
- The factory-provisioning upgrade at the Penang plant was a few weeks late but finished in October; Keystone will reuse its device-identity certificates.

Security notes
Ceremony participants must be from at least two departments. Olu will hold one smart card, Hannah the second, and the third is sealed in the Leeds safe. Backups of the key blob will be stored in both data centers.

Review
This ADR will be revisited after the key ceremony, or earlier if the distributor changes its requirements. Comments go to the #keystone channel.
